newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 26.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
All Papers
INDIA RULING FRONT DEFERS DECISION ON OIL PRICES

Resistance by left-wing parties prevented the ruling United Front from reaching a consensus to raise prices of some oil products to plug a mushrooming oil-subsidy bill. The government was unlikely to take a decision on the issue until the next committee meeting. The outstanding amount, called the oil pool deficit, totaled 155 billion rupees at the end of March.
The Pioneer
INVESTIGATIVE BODY CHIEF REBUTS CHARGES

Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) chief Joginder Singh denied accusations that the agency leaked sensitive information to the press. He also denied that the agency had become a political instrument. Recent newspaper reports indicated the CBI had named slain former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi as an accused in the Howitzer gun deal. Angry MPs demanded Singh be sacked since he had leaked the report to the press.
The Economic Times
DELHI BOURSE CHIEF MAY BE DECLARED DEFAULTER

The bourse regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), has unearthed large-scale irregularities in the transactions of the Delhi bourse (DSE) president. Following an investigation, a DSE board meeting is being convened to take up the issue of defaults by the president in which he is likely to be declared a defaulter. SEBI has received a complaint from a DSE member regarding non-payment of dues by the president amounting to 1.5 million rupees for the purchase of 53,000 shares of Sunrise Securities.
ITC PLANS TO SLASH SUBSIDIARIES

The ITC management is planning to slash the number of subsidiaries and associate companies to enforce corporate governance in group companies. The management plans to divest its holding in some subsidiaries as well as wind up those which no longer serve a worthwhile purpose. Amalgamation of two or more such companies is also on the cards. Currently, the group has 106 subsidiaries and associate companies.
NEW TENDER LIKELY FOR BANGALORE AIRPORT

The issue of the proposed international airport in Bangalore will be taken up at the prime minister's office. A meeting was held between civil aviation secretary and principal secretary. It was decided that the only solution to the deadlock was to re-tender with a new set of conditions. While this throws Tata Industries' foray into the aviation sector into further uncertainty, it is felt that legally it is not possible to alter a build-own-operate model into a build-operate-transfer (BOT) format.
Financial Express
ERICSSON SEES HIGH VOLUMES, FALLING MARGINS

Huge volumes, falling prices, heavy competition and a declining profit margin are what Ericsson envisages in the next couple of years in the fast growing Indian cellular market. Already Ericsson is predicting a 50 percent drop in the price of cellular phones. At the present rate, the consolidated price of a handset varies between 43,000 rupees and 10,000 rupees depending on the make. There are 12 models available and each major company has introduced an average of three models. The pace of growth of the cellular market in India has, in fact, baffled the international players.
INDUSTRY MINISTRY 'DISOWNS' DISINVESTMENT COMMISSION

Irked by the lack of control over the disinvestment commission, the Industry Ministry has asked the Finance Ministry to take this advisory body under its jurisdiction. The commission seems to be facing another storm as Industry Ministry sources virtually disown it saying they cannot be accountable for something over which they have no authority. Stating that decision-making powers over the commission's recommendations rested with the Finance Ministry, sources said the Industry Ministry had asked the Finance Ministry to take over the commission.
Business Standard
NEW BODY TO MONITOR NBFCS ON THE CARDS

The Finance Ministry is considering the institution of a corporate body to monitor the activities of all registered non-banking finance companies. The body will report to the Reserve Bank (RBI). The ministry's plan to set up the corporate body is part of a series of measures that are being considered to plug the systematic loopholes that led to the CRB Capital Markets case. The Reserve Bank of India is expected to add its inputs to the list of measures drawn up by the ministry, following the RBI governor's closed-door meeting with the finance minister.
GOVERNMENT FEARS BIG TAX LOSSES

The public sector oil companies are among several corporates which have deferred their tax liabilities for 1996/97 to the next fiscal year. The revenue department estimates the loss of revenues owing to deferrment of tax liabilities at 10 billion rupees. The estimates have been arrived at on the basis of advance tax collections received through December 1996. Corporates are required to pay up to three quarters of their advance tax instalments by December.
The Observer
INFLATION UP MARGINALLY AFTER 10 WEEKS

For the first time in 10 weeks, the rate of inflation rose marginally to 6.04 percent during the week ended May 10. The annual rate of increase in prices, based on the wholesale price index, rose by 0.06 percentage point to 6.04 percent, from 5.98 percent in the previous week. The index (provisional) for all commodities (base 1981/82/100) also moved up by 0.2 point during the week to 322.8 as against 322.3.
NON BANKING FINANCIERS MAY HAVE TO DISCLOSE VARYING RATINGS

A move is afoot to make it mandatory for non-banking financial companies to disclose different ratings given by credit rating agencies on their various financial instruments. The Reserve Bank (RBI) move is a direct fallout of the CRB caps fiasco. While the RBI is closely looking at this and other ways to check a repeat of the CRB Caps episode, the capital market regulator, SEBI, is debating whether to make ratings mandatory for the financial instruments of manufacturing companies.
MINISTRY TO GET INDEPENDENT REPORT ON SCAM

The Finance Ministry is sending a top bureaucrat to Bombay to get the full details of the CRB Capitals case. The official will submit a report within a week. He is expected to meet officials from the Reserve Bank and the bourse regulator SEBI, and piece together the events. The Finance Ministry believes the CRB issue should not be allowed to continue indefinitely.
